'''Paul Workman''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE|FRS|FRSC|FMedSci}} (born 30 March 1952) is a British scientist noted for his work on the discovery and development of pharmaceutical agents in the field of [[oncology]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Workman|first1=Paul|chapter=Introduction |title=New Approaches in Cancer Pharmacology: Drug Design and Development|date=1994|pages=1–4|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-79088-1_1|publisher=Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg|language=en|isbn=978-3-642-79090-4}}</ref> He was [https://www.icr.ac.uk/about-us/how-we-are-structured/our-leadership-team President and CEO] of [[Institute of Cancer Research|The Institute of Cancer Research]] in London from 2014 to 2021.

==Education and early life==
[[File:Professor Paul Workman FRS.png|thumb|right|Paul Workman]]
Workman was born on 30 March 1952 in [[Workington]], [[Cumbria]], England.<ref name="Who's Who 2016">{{cite web|title=WORKMAN, Prof. Paul|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U284898|website=Who's Who 2016|publisher=Oxford University Press|accessdate=14 October 2016|date=November 2015}}</ref> He was educated at Workington County Grammar School, Cumbria, and completed his [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree in [[Biochemistry]] at the [[University of Leicester]] and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in Cancer Pharmacology at the [[University of Leeds]].  He later received an [[Doctor of Science|Honorary DSc]] degree from the University of Leicester in 2009.

==Career and research==
The early part of his career (1976–90) was spent establishing and leading the Pharmacology and New Drug Development Laboratory at the [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]]'s Clinical Oncology Unit at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he developed new treatments to exploit hypoxic cells in solid tumours and elucidated the enzymes involved in the activation of hypoxia-targeted drugs.<ref name="autogenerated2"/>

In 1990 Workman spent a sabbatical period in the Department of Therapeutic Radiology, [[Stanford University]] and SRI International, California, USA where he continued his work on tumour hypoxia funded by a Fellowship from what was then the [[International Union Against Cancer]].

In 1991 Workman was appointed as a Cancer Research Campaign (CRC) Life Fellow, Professor of Experimental Cancer Therapy, University of Glasgow and Director of Laboratory Research in the CRC Department of Medical Oncology, CRC Beatson Laboratories, Glasgow.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Paul Workman moves to Glasgow|url=http://annonc.oxfordjournals.org/content/2/5/314.full.pdf |journal=Annals of Oncology News |publisher=[[Annals of Oncology]] |date=1991 | volume=2 |issue=5 |pages= 314–319 |accessdate=8 July 2014 }}{{dead link|date=May 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Here he extended his research on tumour hypoxia and molecular targeted therapies.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Chau|first1=Noan-Minh|last2=Rogers|first2=Paul|last3=Aherne|first3=Wynne|last4=Carroll|first4=Veronica|last5=Collins|first5=Ian|last6=McDonald|first6=Edward|last7=Workman|first7=Paul|last8=Ashcroft|first8=Margaret|title=Identification of Novel Small Molecule Inhibitors of Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1 That Differentially Block Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1 Activity and Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Induction in Response to Hypoxic Stress and Growth Factors|journal=Cancer Research|date=1 June 2005|volume=65|issue=11|pages=4918–4928|doi=10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-04-4453|pmid=15930314|language=en|issn=0008-5472|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Workman|first1=Paul|title=Cancer Chemoprevention|date=2004|doi=10.1007/978-1-59259-767-3_22|publisher=Humana Press, Totowa, NJ|isbn=9781617373428|pages=325–337|language=en|chapter=Pharmacological Intervention With Multistep Oncogenesis}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Workman|first1=Paul|title=Principles of Molecular Oncology|pages=421–438|chapter=Emerging Molecular Therapies: Small-Molecule Drugs|oclc=890636199}}</ref>{{page needed|date=October 2018}} Workman also continued his service for the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) as Chairman of the EORTC Pharmacology and Molecular Mechanisms Group. Member of EORTC Board and Council as Chairman of the EORTC New Drug Development Coordinating Committee.<ref>{{cite journal  |url=http://cancerres.aacrjournals.org/content/48/11/3297.full.pdf |title=Cancer Research announcements |journal=Cancer Research |date=1988 |volume=48 |pages=3297–3298 |accessdate=8 July 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |url=http://annonc.oxfordjournals.org/content/5/suppl_5/7.full.pdf |title=History of NCI-EORTC collaboration |publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers |date=1994 |volume= 5 |pages=7–16 |accessdate=8 July 2014|journal=Annals of Oncology |issue=suppl 5 |doi=10.1093/annonc/5.suppl_5.7 }}{{dead link|date=May 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Workman joined the [[Institute of Cancer Research|ICR]] in 1997 to develop its [[Cancer Research UK]] Cancer Therapeutics Unit.<ref name="autogenerated2"/> Overall, since 2005, the Cancer Therapeutic Unit has discovered 17 drug candidates, seven of which have progressed to the patient trial stage. Workman has attributed this record to "taking early academic risks, combining academic and pharmaceutical expertise, and implementing strong leadership and project management. Other contributing factors include running multiple projects on a competitive scale, establishing long-term financial support and – most important – selecting productive and timely industrial collaborations."<ref>{{cite journal |title=Academia and industry: Successes for UK cancer partnership |journal=Nature |date=11 June 2014 |volume=510 |issue=7504 |doi=10.1038/510218d |pmid=24919912 |page=218|last1=Workman |first1=Paul |bibcode=2014Natur.510..218W |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Workman was appointed Deputy CEO of the [[Institute of Cancer Research|ICR]] in March 2011.<ref name="autogenerated2">{{cite web |url=http://www.icr.ac.uk/research/team_leaders/Workman_Paul/index.shtml |title=Professor Paul Workman |publisher=Icr.ac.uk |accessdate=4 April 2012 }}</ref> He was later elected as President and CEO in November 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Workman|first=Paul|date=24 November 2014|title=Professor Paul Workman has been appointed as Chief Executive and President of The Institute of Cancer Research, London, on a permanent basis|url=https://www.icr.ac.uk/news-archive/professor-paul-workman-appointed-as-icr-chief-executive}}</ref>

Workman is currently working on drugs that block molecules essential for the growth and survival of [[cancer cell]]s, in particular, molecular chaperones such as [[Hsp90]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Powers|first1=Marissa V.|last2=Workman|first2=Paul|title=Encyclopedia of Cancer|date=2015|doi=10.1007/978-3-662-46875-3_3810|publisher=Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg|pages=2894–2898|language=en|chapter=Molecular Chaperones|isbn=978-3-662-46874-6}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Workman|first1=Paul|title=Preface [Hot topic:Hsp90 Molecular Chaperone Inhibitors: Opportunities and Challenges (Guest Editor: Paul Workman)]|journal=[[Current Cancer Drug Targets]]|date=30 September 2003|volume=3|issue=5|pages=i|doi=10.2174/1568009033481840|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |url=http://ecancer.org/tv/pubdate/773 |title=SABCS 2010: Molecular chaperones: cancer dependence and druggability – Prof Paul Workman – The Institute of Cancer Research, Sutton, UK |publisher=Ecancer.org |accessdate=4 April 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The leading Hsp90 inhibitor was discovered by Workman's team at ICR in collaboration with Vernalis.<ref>{{cite journal |journal =Cancer Research |date= 15 April 2008 |pmid=18413753 | doi=10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-07-5256 |volume=68 |issue=8 |title=NVP-AUY922: a novel heat shock protein 90 inhibitor active against xenograft tumor growth, angiogenesis, and metastasis |pages=2850–60 | last1 = Eccles | first1 = SA | last2 = Massey | first2 = A | last3 = Raynaud | first3 = FI | doi-access =free }}</ref>
